To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
somatic arginine (Arg)-to-histidine (His) mutations confer a gain-of-function phenotype in the presence of a high intracellular pH (high pHi) that is characteristic of many cancer cells.
cancer-associated arginine-to- histidine mutations confer a pH-sensitive gain of function on mutant proteins and that this effect is dependent on intracellular pH.
somatic mutations confer pH sensing not observed with wild-type proteins and that increased pHi enables the tumorigenic behavior caused by these somatic mutations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the intracellular pH (or pHi) of cancer cells is higher than that of their normal counterparts and how the higher pHi can enhance proliferation and cell survival of cancer cells, thereby promoting tumor growth and metastasis.
the effect of intracellular pH on the activity of mutant proteins that have an arginine to histidine substitution, which is a common cancer-associated mutation.
understanding the mechanisms by which cancer cells adapt to a high pH environment and how these adaptations can be used to target tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cancer cells are characterized by a high intracellular pH, which enables the oncogenic effect of Arg-to-Histidine mutations in various proteins.
cancer cells have higher intracellular pH than normal cells.
the high pH in cancer cells confers oncogenic properties to mutant proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer cells have a higher pH and this higher pH allows for the oncogenic effects to occur.
the intracellular pH in most cancers is constitutive and higher than that of the normal cells.
cancer cells are characterized by high intracellular pH, which enables the tumorigenic behavior conferred by Arg-to-His mutants in proteins such as EGFR and p53.
The main takeaway from our work is that
some somatic cancer mutations may confer a growth advantage to tumor cells by sensing high pHi.
the pH of cancer cells is high and enables the oncogenic properties of some somatic cancer mutations.

cancer cells with high intracellular pH (which is a common characteristic of cancer cells) can be targeted by drugs that decrease pH or by drugs that specifically target pH-sensitive mutant forms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors.
